name: tabl
title: Tabl
notes: Sound-alike: Davul page: 'The Tabl, tapan, atabal or davul is a large double-headed drum that is played with mallets'; 'These drums have both a deep bass sound and a thin treble sound'. The Tabl page (a list page, the name only) also gives it as a Persian name for the tabla; this row follows the Davul page. The davul row above is a sound-alike of the dhol row, which is the nearest

title: Gran cassa
notes: Another name for the orchestral bass drum: the Gran cassa page redirects to the Bass drum page, which says 'the orchestral, or concert bass drum (in Italian: gran cassa, gran tamburo). It is the largest drum of the orchestra'. The same drum (the catalog orchestral bass drum)

name: timbal
title: Timbal (timbau)
notes: Sound-alike: the Timbal page redirects to the Timbau page: 'The timbau or Brazilian timbal is a membranophone instrument derived from the caxambu drum, usually played with both hands'; 'It is played in a similar manner to the atabaque'; 'The sound of the timbau varies from a clear, well-defined, high tone to a strong, deep bass'. The audit gives timbale as the target, but the timbal the page names is the Brazilian timbau, a conical hand drum played like the atabaque (the atabaque row above is a sound-alike of conga). The catalog conga is the nearest

name: tabor pipe drum
title: Tabor pipe drum
notes: No fetched source shows the name. Pipe and tabor page: 'Pipe and tabor is a pair of instruments played by a single player, consisting of a  three-hole pipe played with one hand, and a small drum played with the other'; 'Tabor pipes are widespread throughout the globe'. The pair is "pipe and tabor", and a "tabor pipe" is the pipe (an aerophone), not a drum. The drum is the tabor row above

title: Tumbak
notes: No fetched source shows the name for a drum: the Wikipedia title Tumbak redirects to Tonbak, Iran: 'is a village in Howmeh Rural District'. Greater Kashmir (https://www.greaterkashmir.com/news/opinion/clay-musical-instruments-of-kashmir/) gives the Iranian names as 'In Iran, this instrument is called Tumbakh or Tunbak', not tumbak; the tombak row above covers the drum

name: tumbaknari
title: Tumbaknari
notes: Sound-alike: Outlook India: 'a goblet drum traditional to Jammu and Kashmir'. Greater Kashmir: 'Tumbaknari is struck by the fingertips'; 'in Kashmir, it is still being made of baked clay'. A baked-clay goblet drum struck with the fingertips, a Kashmiri form of the tombak; the catalog darbuka doum (a clay goblet drum's bass stroke) is the nearest, as for the tombak row above
